name: adversarial_ensemble_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, simultaneous agreement across five independent microstructure signals — VWAP dislocation (short-term supply/demand imbalance), ORB directional break (institutional positioning established in the opening 20-minute window), RSI extreme (3-minute momentum exhaustion or initiation), volume spike on a directional bar (block trade or basket execution activity), and EMA trend alignment (10-minute institutional trend context) — indicates a program trade, FII basket order, or multi-strategy algo convergence is in progress. At 5-second resolution, this multi-signal confluence is rare (~2-4 times per session) but highly directional: when all signals agree and none contradicts, NIFTY typically sustains the move for 15-25 spot points over the next 30-120 seconds as the underlying institutional order continues to execute. The adversarial veto eliminates entries where any sub-strategy is actively signaling the opposite direction, filtering out fake breakouts driven by temporary liquidity gaps in the NIFTY order book.

indicators.name: vwap_zscore
indicators.formula: dev = close - session_VWAP; vwap_z = dev / rolling_std(dev, 360)
indicators.purpose: Session VWAP is cumulative — no period scaling needed. The 360-bar (30-min) rolling stddev of deviation captures the current session's volatility regime for normalization, not all-day history. Threshold 1.5σ signals a meaningful dislocation where VWAP-benchmarked algos start aggressively reversing.

indicators.name: orb_high_low
indicators.formula: orb_high = max(high, first 240 bars of day); orb_low = min(low, first 240 bars of day)
indicators.purpose: Fixed time window (09:15-09:35 IST = 20 minutes = 240 bars). Not scaled — the opening range is defined by calendar time, not bar count. Same 20-min window as the original but now resolved at 5-second granularity, allowing entry immediately on breakout rather than waiting for the next 1-min bar close.

indicators.name: rsi_36
indicators.purpose: Original uses 40-bar RSI on 1-min bars (40-minute RSI). We target 30-120 second holds — the relevant exhaustion signal is the 3-minute momentum shift, not the 40-minute one. RSI(36) = 3-minute RSI detects when a fast directional push has created a short-term extreme. Threshold 35/65 (vs standard 30/70) is more sensitive to fast 5-second data.

indicators.name: volume_spike
indicators.formula: vol_spike = volume > vol_ratio * rolling_mean(volume, 60); dir = +1 if close>open, -1 if close<open
indicators.purpose: Original uses 20-bar (20-minute) volume baseline on 1-min bars. Compressed to 60-bar (5-minute) baseline to match the faster hold time — 5 minutes of volume history is sufficient context for detecting intrabar block activity. A volume spike on a directional bar at 5s frequency typically indicates a basket trade or large institutional order hitting.

indicators.name: ema_60_120
indicators.formula: ema_120 = EMA(close, 120); ema_60 = EMA(close, 60); ema_cross_up = close crosses above ema_60 while close > ema_120
indicators.purpose: Original uses EMA(20) on 1-min = 20-minute trend context. We use EMA(120) = 10-minute context (same order of magnitude) as trend filter, and EMA(60) = 5-minute as the pullback trigger. A close-above-EMA(60) while above EMA(120) detects micro-pullback entries in established intraday trends — the same thesis as the original but adapted to 5-second resolution.

conditions: no sub-strategy is -1 (adversarial veto: no active contradiction)
condition holds for 2 consecutive bars (10-second persistence, filters single-bar spikes)
buy_ce.confirmation: 2-bar persistence required on all conditions simultaneously

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option pts = ~8 NIFTY spot pts at delta 0.5. When 3+ sub-strategies agree and the signal is wrong, NIFTY typically stalls and reverses within 30 seconds — a move of 8 spot pts against within the first 30s means the institutional order has already completed or the signal was spurious. Tighter than deep-reversion strategies because this is a high-conviction entry, not a mean-reversion with a final-flush risk.
exit.target_rationale: 7 option pts = ~14 NIFTY spot pts at delta 0.5. FII basket executions and program trades on NIFTY typically run 15-25 spot points over 30-90 seconds; 14 pts captures the lower bound (conservative) of the expected directional move. At 1:1.75 R:R with 55%+ win rate, this is profitable after all costs.

filters.vix_filter: vix_close < 22.0 (ensemble signals are less reliable in extreme vol regimes where sub-strategy correlations spike)
filters.time_filter: 09:20-15:25 IST; first 5 minutes skipped to allow ORB to begin forming
filters.spread_filter: not required — limit order execution at candle close

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — multi-signal adversarial ensemble is structurally robust; sub-strategies must all degrade simultaneously for edge to disappear. However, in low-volatility regimes signals will be rare.

adaptation_notes: Original trades top-20 NIFTY50 stocks on 1-min bars, hold 15-60 minutes. Converted to NIFTY index 5-sec bars, hold 30-120 seconds. Key changes: (1) ORB window unchanged in calendar time (20 min) but resolves faster. (2) RSI compressed from 40-bar/40-min to 36-bar/3-min — we catch fast momentum, not slow divergence. (3) Volume baseline compressed from 20-bar/20-min to 60-bar/5-min. (4) EMA from 20-bar/20-min to 120-bar/10-min (same order of magnitude). (5) 2-bar persistence check = 10 seconds (original was 2 bars at 1-min = 2 minutes — same ratio relative to hold time). (6) Stops/targets in option premium points not percentage-based. The adversarial veto logic is preserved intact — it's the unique structural element that differentiates this from single-signal strategies.
weaknesses: Very low signal frequency — 3/5 agreement with no contradiction fires 2-4 times per session; statistically meaningful only over many weeks
Sub-strategies can be correlated on NIFTY (VWAP reversion and RSI extreme often fire together on the same directional push), reducing true ensemble diversity
ORB signal is directionally binary after the first 20 min — if NIFTY breaks out early, ORB stays +1 for rest of day and may over-contribute to ensemble in the original breakout direction
Loop-based VWAP and ORB computation is O(n) — acceptable but slower than vectorized alternatives
